source.text: Ἐγένετο τότε τὰ ἐγκαίνια ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις· χειμὼν ἦν, καὶ περιεπάτει ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τοῦ Σολομῶνος.

records.literal_gloss: Took place then the Dedication in the Jerusalem; winter it was, \v 23 and was walking the Jesus in the temple in the colonnade of the Solomon.

en.L: At that time the [Feast of] Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter, \v 23 and Jesus was walking in the temple, in the colonnade of Solomon.
en.B: Then came the time of the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem. It was winter, \v 23 and Jesus was walking about in the temple courts, in Solomon's Colonnade.
en.R: Then it was time for the Feast of Dedication, also called Hanukkah, in Jerusalem. It was winter. \v 23 Jesus was walking in the temple area, along the covered walkway called Solomon's Colonnade.

es.L: Se celebraba entonces en Jerusalén la [fiesta de la] Dedicación. Era invierno, \v 23 y Jesús andaba en el templo, en el pórtico de Salomón.
es.B: Llegó entonces la fiesta de la Dedicación en Jerusalén. Era invierno, \v 23 y Jesús andaba por los atrios del templo, en el pórtico de Salomón.
es.R: Entonces llegó en Jerusalén la fiesta de la Dedicación, también llamada Janucá. Era invierno. \v 23 Jesús caminaba por el patio del templo, por el corredor cubierto llamado pórtico de Salomón.

fr.L: Alors eut lieu la [fête de la] Dédicace à Jérusalem. C’était l’hiver, \v 23 et Jésus marchait dans le temple, sous le portique de Salomon.
fr.B: Vint alors la fête de la Dédicace, à Jérusalem. C’était l’hiver, \v 23 et Jésus allait et venait dans la cour du temple, sous le portique de Salomon.
fr.R: Ensuite, à Jérusalem, c’était la fête de la Dédicace, qu’on appelle aussi Hanoukka. C’était l’hiver. \v 23 Jésus marchait dans la cour du temple, sous la galerie couverte appelée portique de Salomon.

sw.L: Wakati huo [Sikukuu ya] Kuweka Wakfu ilifanyika huko Yerusalemu. Ilikuwa majira ya baridi, \v 23 naye Yesu alikuwa akitembea hekaluni, katika ukumbi wa Solomoni.
sw.B: Kisha ukafika wakati wa Sikukuu ya Kuweka Wakfu huko Yerusalemu. Ilikuwa majira ya baridi, \v 23 naye Yesu alikuwa akitembea katika nyua za hekalu, katika Ukumbi wa Solomoni.
sw.R: Kisha ukafika wakati wa Sikukuu ya Kuweka Wakfu Hekalu, inayoitwa pia Hanuka, huko Yerusalemu. Ilikuwa majira ya baridi. \v 23 Yesu alikuwa akitembea katika uwanja wa hekalu, kando ya njia yenye paa iitwayo Ukumbi wa Solomoni.

vi.L: Lúc ấy là [lễ] Cung Hiến tại Giê-ru-sa-lem. Bấy giờ là mùa đông, \v 23 và Đức Giê-xu đang đi lại trong đền thờ, ở hành lang của Sa-lô-môn.
vi.B: Bấy giờ đến kỳ lễ Cung Hiến tại Giê-ru-sa-lem. Lúc đó là mùa đông, \v 23 và Đức Giê-xu đang đi lại trong sân đền thờ, nơi Hành Lang Sa-lô-môn.
vi.R: Bấy giờ là dịp lễ Cung Hiến, cũng gọi là lễ Ha-nu-ca, tại Giê-ru-sa-lem. Lúc đó là mùa đông. \v 23 Đức Giê-xu đang đi trong sân đền thờ, dọc theo dãy hành lang có mái che gọi là Hành Lang Sa-lô-môn.

ko.L: 그때에 예루살렘에서 수전절이 있었다. 겨울이었다. \v 23 그리고 예수께서 성전 안 솔로몬의 주랑에서 거닐고 계셨다.
ko.B: 그 무렵 예루살렘에서 성전 봉헌절이 되었다. 때는 겨울이었다. \v 23 예수께서는 성전 뜰에 있는 솔로몬 주랑을 거닐고 계셨다.
ko.R: 그때 예루살렘에서는 하누카라고도 하는 성전 봉헌절이 되었다. 겨울이었다. \v 23 예수께서는 성전 뜰에서, 솔로몬 주랑이라고 부르는 지붕 덮인 긴 복도를 걷고 계셨다.

pt.L: Naquele tempo aconteceu em Jerusalém a [festa da] Dedicação. Era inverno, \v 23 e Jesus andava no templo, na colunata de Salomão.
pt.B: Chegou então a época da festa da Dedicação em Jerusalém. Era inverno, \v 23 e Jesus andava pelos pátios do templo, no Pórtico de Salomão.
pt.R: Chegou o tempo da festa da Dedicação, também chamada Hanucá, em Jerusalém. Era inverno. \v 23 Jesus estava andando na área do templo, pelo corredor coberto que se chamava Pórtico de Salomão.

decisions.choice: the Dedication: the festival remembering the rededication of the temple, known today as Hanukkah
decisions.reason: The word means a dedication or renewal. In 167 BC the Syrian king Antiochus IV set up pagan worship in the temple at Jerusalem. After Judas Maccabeus and his followers took the city back, they cleansed the temple and dedicated a new altar in December 164 BC, and decreed that the day be kept each year for eight days (1 Maccabees 4:36-59; 2 Maccabees 10:1-8). Unlike Passover and Tabernacles, it was not one of the festivals commanded in the Law of Moses. John names it as he names the other festivals (2:13; 7:2).

decisions.choice: it was winter: the festival fell in December
decisions.reason: The festival began on the twenty-fifth day of the month Kislev (1 Maccabees 4:52), which falls in December. The note dates the scene some two months after the Feast of Tabernacles of chapter 7, and it may explain why Jesus was in the covered colonnade rather than in the open courts. John does not say so, and no level adds it.

decisions.choice: the colonnade of Solomon: a roofed walkway on the east side of the temple courts
alternatives: a porch at the entrance of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word is used of a long colonnade: a row of columns carrying a roof, open on one side. Herod's temple courts were surrounded by colonnades, and the one along the east side was called Solomon's, after the builder of the first temple; the Jewish historian Josephus describes it. The first believers later met there (Acts 3:11; 5:12). It was a public place where teachers walked and talked with people.

decisions.choice: a festival of the temple's dedication as the setting for what Jesus says
decisions.reason: John sets these words at the feast that celebrated the consecration of the temple. Later in the same exchange Jesus speaks of himself as the one whom the Father consecrated and sent into the world (10:36), and earlier John has called his body a temple (2:19-21). The setting may be meant to bring these together, but John does not draw the link himself.

decisions.choice: temple courts (B); temple area (R)
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area, with its courts and colonnades, not the sanctuary itself (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: also called Hanukkah; covered walkway
decisions.reason: Readable gives the festival the name most readers know today (meaning decision m1) and says what a colonnade is: a roofed walkway (meaning decision m3). "Hanukkah" is the Hebrew word for dedication, so the name adds nothing John does not say. Readable also breaks the record into short sentences.

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The 2:14 choice for the whole temple area.

decisions.choice: también llamada Janucá; corredor cubierto
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable gives the name most readers know (meaning decision m1) and says what a colonnade was (m3).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level; the imperfect for what was going on ("marchait", "disaient") at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (10:22-30), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("eut lieu", "entourèrent", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus a répondu"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. The imperfect describes the scene at every level: Jesus walking in the colonnade, the questioners pressing him.

decisions.choice: qu’on appelle aussi Hanoukka; la galerie couverte appelée portique de Salomon
decisions.reason: As in the English Readable, the festival is given the name most readers know (meaning decision m1) and the colonnade is described (m3). "Hanoukka" is the usual French spelling. "Portique" is kept at every level as the name of the place, with "galerie couverte" saying what it was.

decisions.choice: Sikukuu ya Kuweka Wakfu
decisions.reason: The festival remembered the rededication of the temple. "Kuweka wakfu" (to dedicate, set apart for God) is the plain modern phrase; "kutabaruku" is the older Bible word, which few readers know.

decisions.choice: "lễ Cung Hiến" for the Dedication; R adds "lễ Ha-nu-ca"
decisions.reason: "Cung Hiến" is the usual Vietnamese church word for a dedication; "Ha-nu-ca" transliterates Hanukkah in the hyphenated style of the guide's names. Neither is in the style guide.

decisions.choice: "đền thờ" (L), "sân đền thờ" (B, R) for hieron; "hành lang" for the colonnade
decisions.reason: As the style guide's temple entry. "hành lang" names a roofed walkway; R adds "có mái che" to make the picture plain.

decisions.choice: "수전절" (L); "성전 봉헌절" (B, R), with "하누카" at R
decisions.reason: "수전절" is the established Protestant name of the feast but is opaque to most readers today; Balanced and Readable say what it celebrated, and Readable adds its modern Jewish name, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "성전 안" (L); "성전 뜰" (B, R); "솔로몬의 주랑" (L), "솔로몬 주랑" (B, R)
decisions.reason: hieron is the whole temple area (book-wide choice). "주랑" (colonnade) is the current word; the older "행각" is little understood now.

decisions.choice: a colunata de Salomão (L); o Pórtico de Salomão (B, R); Hanucá (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain architectural word "colunata", a row of columns carrying a roof (meaning decision m3). Balanced and Readable use "Pórtico", the usual Portuguese name for such a covered walkway, capitalised as the name of a place; Readable also says what it is, "corredor coberto". "Hanucá" is the spelling most Brazilian Jewish and general usage gives the feast.

source.text: ἐκύκλωσαν οὖν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἕως πότε τὴν ψυχὴν ἡμῶν αἴρεις;

records.literal_gloss: Surrounded therefore him the Jews and were saying to him, "Until when the soul of us you lift?

en.L: So the Jews surrounded {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and were saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "How long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hold our soul in suspense?
en.B: So the Jews who were there surrounded {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "How long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} leave us in suspense?
en.R: The Jews who were there crowded around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "How long are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going to keep us guessing?

es.L: Lo rodearon, pues, los judíos y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} decían: «¿Hasta cuándo tendrás en vilo nuestra alma?
es.B: Entonces los judíos que estaban allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} rodearon y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿Hasta cuándo nos vas a tener en suspenso?
es.R: Los judíos que estaban allí se juntaron a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor. Le preguntaron: «¿Hasta cuándo nos vas a tener con la duda?

fr.L: Les Juifs {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entourèrent donc et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disaient : « Jusqu’à quand tiendras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} notre âme en suspens ?
fr.B: Les Juifs qui étaient là {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entourèrent alors et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Jusqu’à quand vas-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous laisser dans l’incertitude ?
fr.R: Les Juifs qui étaient là se sont rassemblés autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Jusqu’à quand est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vas nous laisser dans le doute ?

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi wakamzunguka, wakawa wakimwambia, "Mpaka lini utaishika roho yetu mashakani?
sw.B: Basi Wayahudi waliokuwa pale wakamzunguka, wakamwambia, "Utatuacha katika wasiwasi mpaka lini?
sw.R: Wayahudi waliokuwa pale walimzunguka. Wakamwuliza, "Utaendelea kututatanisha mpaka lini?

vi.L: Vậy người Do Thái vây quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và cứ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông còn giữ hồn chúng tôi lơ lửng cho đến bao giờ?
vi.B: Vậy những người Do Thái ở đó vây quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Ông còn để chúng tôi phân vân đến bao giờ?
vi.R: Những người Do Thái ở đó xúm lại quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông còn bắt chúng tôi đoán mãi đến bao giờ?

ko.L: 그러자 유대인들이 그분을 둘러싸고 그분께 말하고 있었다. "언제까지 우리 영혼을 매달아 둘 셈이냐?
ko.B: 그러자 그곳에 있던 유대인들이 그분을 둘러싸고 말했다. "언제까지 우리 마음을 졸이게 할 작정이냐?
ko.R: 그곳에 있던 유대인들이 예수를 에워쌌다. 그리고 그분께 물었다. "언제까지 우리 애를 태울 셈이냐?

pt.L: Então os judeus {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} cercaram e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} diziam: "Até quando manterás a nossa alma em suspenso?
pt.B: Então os judeus que estavam ali {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} cercaram e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disseram: "Até quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nos deixarás em suspense?
pt.R: Os judeus que estavam ali se juntaram em volta de Jesus. Eles perguntaram a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}: "Até quando vais nos deixar sem saber?

decisions.choice: the Jews: the hostile hearers who gathered around Jesus in the temple
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: These questioners are hostile: Jesus tells them that they do not believe and are not his sheep (10:25-26), and in 10:31 and 10:39 they try to stone and to seize him for blasphemy, as had happened before (5:18; 8:59). Their demand sounds like the authorities' questions (1:19; 8:13), and leaders may well have been among them, but John does not single them out. The word names this group of hearers, not the people as a whole: Jesus, his disciples and the many who believe in him (10:42) are Jews.

decisions.choice: surrounded: they closed in around him
alternatives: gathered near him in a friendly way
decisions.reason: The verb means to encircle. It is used of armies surrounding a city (Luke 21:20). Here it pictures Jesus hemmed in by a group demanding an answer, in the colonnade where he was walking.

decisions.choice: how long will you keep us in suspense: their minds are held up, waiting for an answer
alternatives: how long will you trouble or annoy us
how long will you take away our life
decisions.reason: Word for word they say, "How long do you lift up our soul?" The phrase can mean to stir up someone's hopes or keep them hanging in uncertainty, and that fits the demand that follows, "tell us plainly" (10:24b). In later Greek a similar phrase can mean to vex or annoy someone, and the questioners may mean that too: they are impatient, not simply curious.

decisions.choice: the Jews who were there (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the group of hearers in the temple (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:48 and 10:31 do, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me", "my" and "mine" when Jesus speaks of himself, and "you" when others speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" or "My" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: hold our soul in suspense (L); leave us in suspense (B); keep us guessing (R)
alternatives: lift up our soul (word for word)
decisions.reason: Word for word the phrase would suggest lifting up the soul in prayer, as in Psalm 25:1, which is not meant here. Literal keeps "soul" and supplies the sense of the idiom; Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los judíos que estaban allí / que lo habían rodeado (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers gathered around Jesus in the temple (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the people as a whole, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: tendrás en vilo nuestra alma (L); en suspenso (B); con la duda (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the phrase means keeping them waiting for an answer (meaning decision m3), not lifting up the soul in prayer. Every plural "you" in this passage is the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les Juifs qui étaient là (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word names this group of hostile hearers in the temple (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the whole people. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people present, as the English does, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew; Jesus and his disciples are Jews too.

decisions.choice: tenir notre âme en suspens (L); nous laisser dans l’incertitude (B); nous laisser dans le doute (R)
alternatives: Jusqu’à quand tiendras-tu nos esprits en haleine ?
decisions.reason: Word for word the Greek says "lift our soul", which in French, as in English, would suggest prayer (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "âme" and gives the sense with "en suspens"; Balanced and Readable use everyday phrases for being kept waiting for an answer.

decisions.choice: "những người Do Thái ở đó" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision names the hostile hearers gathered around Jesus, not specifically the authorities, so B and R follow the English "the Jews who were there".

decisions.choice: "ông" for "you" in the hostile hearers' mouths, with no deity_pronoun span; "chúng tôi" for themselves
alternatives: "Ngài" with the span, as the English has its span
decisions.reason: Style guide section 6: those who reject Jesus address him as "ông"; Vietnamese has no reverent form they would use, so the setting does not apply in their speech in 10:24-33.

decisions.choice: "giữ hồn chúng tôi lơ lửng" for "hold our soul in suspense"
decisions.reason: Keeps the Greek word "soul" (hồn) at Literal in a phrase Vietnamese can still read; B and R give the sense.

decisions.choice: The hostile hearers speak to Jesus without honorifics, in the plain style ("-냐", "네가")
decisions.reason: The style guide lets open opponents address Jesus without honorifics where the scene is hostile: they surround him, and soon pick up stones (10:31). The narrator still uses the honorific for Jesus. This holds through 10:24-33.

decisions.choice: "그곳에 있던 유대인들" (B, R), not "유대 지도자들"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision takes them as the hostile hearers in the temple, not named as the authorities; Balanced and Readable keep "유대인들" and say who they were, as the English does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean ("그분", "께", the honorific -시-)
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: tu (manterás, deixarás, vais)
decisions.reason: As everywhere in the Portuguese, people who speak to Jesus use "tu", his opponents included; the hostility shows in what they say, not in the form of address.

decisions.choice: manterás a nossa alma em suspenso (L); nos deixarás em suspense (B); vais nos deixar sem saber (R)
alternatives: levantas a nossa alma (word for word)
decisions.reason: As in English, the word-for-word phrase would suggest lifting the soul in prayer. Literal keeps "alma" and supplies the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

source.text: εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός, εἰπὲ ἡμῖν παρρησίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: If you are the Christ, tell us plainly."

en.L: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, tell us plainly."
en.B: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, tell us in plain words."
en.R: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, tell us so clearly."

es.B: Si {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, dínoslo con claridad».

sw.B: Ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, tuambie kwa maneno yaliyo wazi."

vi.L: Nếu ông là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, hãy nói thẳng cho chúng tôi."
vi.B: Nếu ông là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, thì hãy nói rõ cho chúng tôi biết."
vi.R: Nếu ông là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} thì hãy nói rõ ràng cho chúng tôi biết đi."

pt.B: Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, dize-nos com palavras claras."
pt.R: Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, fala isso claramente para nós."

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God had promised
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title, not a name: the one God would anoint to rule, whom the people expected (1:20, 41; 7:26-27, 41-42). The question is whether Jesus claims to be that person.

decisions.choice: plainly: in clear words, without figures of speech
decisions.reason: The word can mean speaking in public (7:26) or speaking plainly. Here it is the second: Jesus has been speaking in a figure about the shepherd and the sheep (10:6), and they want a direct yes or no. John uses the word the same way in 11:14 and 16:25, 29, where plain speech is set against figures.

decisions.choice: a demand for a direct claim that Jesus answers by pointing to his works
decisions.reason: In public Jesus has not called himself the Christ in so many words, though he has told the Samaritan woman (4:25-26) and the man born blind (9:35-37) who he is. A plain claim to be the Christ could be heard as a claim to be king, and could be used against him (compare 19:12). Jesus answers that he has already told them, and that his works speak for him (10:25).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Where the Greek has "the Christ" as a title, every level writes "the" before the setting, so that the alternative reads "the Messiah" (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: in plain words (B); clearly (R)
decisions.reason: "Openly" could suggest speaking in public; Balanced and Readable make clear that the questioners want direct speech (meaning decision m2). Readable adds "so" for the yes they want to hear.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: abiertamente (L); con claridad (B); claramente (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "abiertamente" covers both "in public" and "plainly", so Literal keeps the word of 7:4, 13 and 26; Balanced and Readable give the sense here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: franchement (L, B); clairement (R); le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}
decisions.reason: The questioners want plain words rather than figures (meaning decision m2). "Ouvertement" could mean "in public", the other sense of the Greek word; "franchement" says "straight out, without hiding anything". The title has the article, so "le" stands outside the christos setting, as in 1:20. Literal keeps the stressed "toi" of the Greek.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}라면" with no word for "the"
decisions.reason: Korean has no article, and the title reads as a title without one; the ending -라면 suits both 그리스도 and 메시아, so the setting needs no other change.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἶπον ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε· τὰ ἔργα ἃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρός μου ταῦτα μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ·

en.L: Jesus answered them, "I told you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, these testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Jesus answered them, "I have told you, and you do not believe. The works I do in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's name are themselves witnesses for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I already told you, but you do not believe. The things I do with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's authority show you who I am.

es.L: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Se lo|Os lo}} dije, y no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}. Las obras que yo hago en el nombre de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, estas dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

es.R: Jesús respondió: «Ya {{plural_you:se lo dije|os lo dije}}, pero no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}. Las cosas que hago con la autoridad de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre {{plural_you:les|os}} muestran quién soy.

fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Je vous l’ai dit, et vous ne croyez pas. Les œuvres que je fais au nom de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père sont elles-mêmes des témoins en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} faveur.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Je vous l’ai déjà dit, mais vous ne croyez pas. Ce que je fais avec l’autorité de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père vous montre qui je suis.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp lời họ: "Ta đã nói với các người, mà các người không tin. Những việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm nhân danh Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chính những việc ấy làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Ta đã nói với các người, nhưng các người không tin. Chính những việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm nhân danh Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là lời chứng cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ta đã nói rồi, nhưng các người không tin. Những việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm bằng thẩm quyền của Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho các người thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là ai.

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "내가 너희에게 말하였으나 너희는 믿지 않는다. 내가 내 아버지의 이름으로 하는 일들, 그것들이 나에 대하여 증언한다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "내가 이미 말했는데도 너희는 믿지 않는다. 내가 내 아버지의 이름으로 하는 일들이 바로 나에 대하여 증언하고 있다.
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 이미 말했는데도 너희는 믿지 않는다. 내가 내 아버지의 권한으로 하는 일들이 내가 누구인지 너희에게 보여 준다.

pt.L: Jesus lhes respondeu: "Eu lhes disse, e vocês não creem. As obras que eu faço em nome do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, essas dão testemunho a respeito de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.B: Jesus lhes respondeu: "Eu já lhes disse, e vocês não creem. As obras que eu faço em nome do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai são elas mesmas testemunhas a {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} favor.
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "Eu já disse a vocês, mas vocês não acreditam. As coisas que eu faço com a autoridade do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai mostram a vocês quem eu sou.

decisions.choice: I told you: he has made his claim already, though not in the words they demand
alternatives: he had once said in so many words that he is the Christ
decisions.reason: John records no public saying in Jerusalem in which Jesus calls himself the Christ. But he has told them who he is in other words: that God is his own Father (5:17-18), that he is the light of the world (8:12), that before Abraham was, he is (8:58), and that he is the good shepherd (10:11-14). Their unbelief is not for lack of a clear word.

decisions.choice: the works: all that Jesus does, his signs above all
decisions.reason: John uses "works" for Jesus's deeds as the Father's own work done through him (5:17, 36; 9:3-4). They include the signs, such as the healing of the man born blind (9:1-7) that was still being argued about (10:21). Jesus points to them again in 10:32, 37-38 and 14:10-11.

decisions.choice: in the name of my Father: as his representative, with his authority
decisions.reason: To act in someone's name is to act for him, by his authority. Jesus has said that he came in his Father's name (5:43): his works are not his own project but the Father's.

decisions.choice: testify: the language of a witness in court
decisions.reason: John often uses the language of testimony, as in a trial. In 5:31-37 Jesus named the witnesses to him: John the Baptist, his works and the Father himself. The Law required more than one witness (Deuteronomy 19:15; compare 8:17-18). Here the works stand as witnesses in his case.

decisions.choice: are themselves witnesses for me (B); show you who I am, with my Father's authority (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress on "these" and the language of witness (meaning decision m4). Readable says what "in the name of" means (meaning decision m3) and what the testimony is about: who Jesus is, which is the question asked in 10:24.

decisions.choice: son las que dan testimonio de mí (B); con la autoridad de mi Padre ... muestran quién soy (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced keeps the stress on "estas" and the language of witness (meaning decision m4); Readable says what acting in the Father's name means (m3).

decisions.choice: les œuvres (L, B); ce que je fais (R)
decisions.reason: "Les œuvres" is the word French uses for the deeds that show who someone is, and it keeps the thread through John (5:36; 10:32, 37-38; 14:10-11; meaning decision m2); "miracles" would say less than John's word, and "actions" sounds ordinary. Readable says "ce que je fais", as the English Readable says "the things I do".

decisions.choice: "Ta" and "các người" for Jesus and his hearers
decisions.reason: Style guide section 6: Jesus speaks to opponents as "các người" and of himself as "Ta", kept through 10:25-38.

decisions.choice: "증언한다" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The book-wide term for martyreo is "증언하다" (style guide, section 6), the court word for a witness's testimony; the older "증거하다" now means "prove".

source.text: ἀλλὰ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε, ὅτι οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐκ τῶν προβάτων τῶν ἐμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: But you not believe, because not you are of the sheep the mine.

en.L: But you do not believe, because you are not of the sheep that are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.
en.B: But you do not believe, because you are not among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep.

ko.L: 그러나 너희는 믿지 않는다. 너희가 내 양들에 속하지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 내 양이 아니기 때문에 믿지 않는다.
ko.R: 그런데 너희는 내 양이 아니어서 믿지 않는 것이다.

pt.L: Mas vocês não creem, porque não são das ovelhas que são {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}}.
pt.B: Mas vocês não creem, porque não estão entre as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} ovelhas.
pt.R: Mas vocês não acreditam, porque não fazem parte das {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} ovelhas.

decisions.choice: no further words after "my sheep" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: "... my sheep, as I said to you" (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, among them Codex Alexandrinus, Codex Bezae and most later ones, add "as I said to you" at the end of the verse, as the King James Version reflects. The words are not in the oldest papyri or in Codices Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Jesus has not said these exact words before, so a scribe may have added them to point back to 10:14 and 10:16, or attached them to 10:27. A footnote gives the longer reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: because you are not my sheep: belonging and believing go together
alternatives: they are not his sheep because they do not believe
decisions.reason: Jesus gives the reason for their unbelief: they do not belong to his flock. John says elsewhere that those the Father gives to Jesus come to him (6:37, 44, 65), and also that people are answerable for refusing to believe (3:18-19; 8:24; 9:41). The text holds both, as 6:37 does, without explaining how they fit.

decisions.choice: my sheep: the picture of the shepherd from 10:1-16
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the picture he gave earlier: the sheep that know the shepherd's voice (10:3-4) and that he knows (10:14). The words "the sheep that are mine" stress belonging: they are his own.

decisions.choice: among my sheep (B); belong to my sheep (R)
alternatives: of the sheep that are mine (Literal)
decisions.reason: Plain English for being one of the flock that is his (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: de mis ovejas (B); parte de mis ovejas (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for being one of his flock (meaning decision m3).

source.text: τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἐμὰ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούουσιν, κἀγὼ γινώσκω αὐτά, καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσίν μοι, κἀγὼ δίδωμι αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀπόλωνται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ οὐχ ἁρπάσει τις αὐτὰ ἐκ τῆς χειρός μου.

records.literal_gloss: The sheep the mine the voice of me hear, and I know them, and they follow me, \v 28 and I give to them life eternal, and not not they will perish into the age, and not will snatch anyone them out of the hand of me.

en.L: The sheep that are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, and I know them, and they follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \v 28 and I give them eternal life, and they will by no means perish, ever, and no one will snatch them out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

en.R: My sheep listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice. I know them, and they follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 28 I give them eternal life, the life of the age to come, which starts now. They will never be lost. No one will snatch them out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

es.L: Las ovejas {{deity_pronoun:mías|Mías}} oyen {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz, y yo las conozco, y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} siguen, \v 28 y yo les doy vida eterna, y jamás perecerán, y nadie las arrebatará de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano.

es.R: Mis ovejas escuchan {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz. Yo las conozco, y ellas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} siguen. \v 28 Yo les doy vida eterna, la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya. Nunca se perderán. Nadie las arrebatará de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano.

fr.L: Les brebis qui sont les {{deity_pronoun:miennes|Miennes}} écoutent {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je les connais, et elles {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivent, \v 28 et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je leur donne [la] vie éternelle, et elles ne périront absolument jamais, et personne ne les arrachera de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main.
fr.B: Les brebis qui sont à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} écoutent {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix ; je les connais, et elles {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivent. \v 28 Je leur donne la vie éternelle, et elles ne périront jamais. Personne ne les arrachera de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main.
fr.R: Mes brebis écoutent {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix. Je les connais, et elles {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivent. \v 28 Je leur donne la vie éternelle, la vie du monde à venir, qui commence dès maintenant. Elles ne seront jamais perdues. Personne ne les arrachera de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main.

sw.L: Kondoo walio {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} huisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nawajua, nao hunifuata, \v 28 {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nawapa uzima wa milele, nao hakika hawataangamia milele, wala hakuna atakayewanyakua kutoka mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}.
sw.B: Kondoo walio {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} huisikiliza sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; nawajua, nao hunifuata. \v 28 Nawapa uzima wa milele, nao hawataangamia kamwe. Hakuna atakayewanyakua kutoka mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}.
sw.R: Kondoo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} huisikiliza sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Nawajua, nao hunifuata. \v 28 Nawapa uzima wa milele, uzima wa nyakati zijazo, unaoanza sasa. Hawatapotea kamwe. Hakuna atakayewanyakua kutoka mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}.

vi.L: Chiên thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết chúng, và chúng theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \v 28 và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho chúng sự sống đời đời, và chúng nhất định không bao giờ hư mất, và không ai cướp chúng khỏi tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Những chiên thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết chúng, và chúng theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \v 28 Ta ban cho chúng sự sống đời đời, và chúng sẽ không bao giờ hư mất. Không ai cướp được chúng khỏi tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Chiên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lắng nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta biết chúng, và chúng đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \v 28 Ta ban cho chúng sự sống đời đời, là sự sống của thời đại sắp đến, bắt đầu ngay từ bây giờ. Chúng sẽ không bao giờ bị mất. Không ai có thể giật chúng khỏi tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 내 양들은 내 음성을 듣고, 나는 그들을 알며, 그들은 나를 따른다. \v 28 나는 그들에게 영원한 생명을 준다. 그들은 결코 영원히 멸망하지 않을 것이고, 아무도 그들을 내 손에서 낚아채 가지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 내 양들은 내 목소리를 알아듣는다. 나는 그들을 알고, 그들은 나를 따른다. \v 28 나는 그들에게 영원한 생명을 준다. 그들은 결코 멸망하지 않을 것이다. 아무도 그들을 내 손에서 빼앗아 가지 못한다.
ko.R: 내 양들은 내 목소리를 듣는다. 나는 그들을 알고, 그들은 나를 따라온다. \v 28 나는 그들에게 영원한 생명, 곧 다가올 세상의 생명을 준다. 그 생명은 지금부터 시작된다. 그들은 절대로 망하지 않을 것이다. 아무도 그들을 내 손에서 빼앗아 갈 수 없다.

pt.L: As ovelhas que são {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} ouvem a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} voz, e eu as conheço, e elas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} seguem, \v 28 e eu lhes dou a vida eterna, e de modo nenhum elas perecerão, jamais, e ninguém as arrebatará da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão.
pt.B: As ovelhas que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertencem escutam a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} voz; eu as conheço, e elas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} seguem. \v 28 Eu lhes dou a vida eterna, e elas nunca perecerão. Ninguém as arrancará da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão.
pt.R: As {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} ovelhas escutam a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} voz. Eu conheço cada uma delas, e elas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} seguem. \v 28 Eu dou a elas a vida eterna, a vida do mundo que há de vir, que já começa agora. Elas nunca vão se perder. Ninguém vai arrancá-las da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão.

decisions.choice: hear, know, follow: the marks of the sheep in 10:3-5 and 10:14
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats what he said in the picture of the shepherd: the sheep hear his voice and follow him (10:3-4), he knows his own (10:14), and they will not follow a stranger (10:5). Knowing here is personal, like the knowledge between the Father and the Son (10:15).

decisions.choice: they will never perish: a strong denial, for all time
decisions.reason: The Greek joins two negatives, the strongest way to deny that something will happen, and adds "to the age", which means for ever. Together they say that the sheep will not perish at any time. The verb is the one used in 3:16 and in 6:39, where Jesus says he will lose none of those the Father has given him.

decisions.choice: eternal life: a gift given now
decisions.reason: The verb is present: "I give". Eternal life is the life of the age to come, and in John it begins now for those who believe (3:36; 5:24; 6:47, 54).

decisions.choice: snatch out of my hand: take away by force from his keeping
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the wolf that snatches the sheep (10:12). The hand stands for power and protection, as often in Scripture (Deuteronomy 32:39; Isaiah 43:13). No one has the power to take the sheep from Jesus. The same words are used of the Father's hand in 10:29.

decisions.choice: The sheep that belong to me (B); My sheep (R); listen to (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the stress that the Greek puts on "mine" by placing it after the noun; Readable uses the shorter "my". "Listen to" says that hearing here means heeding. Balanced and Readable break the long sentence and leave out the repeated "and".

decisions.choice: the life of the age to come, which starts now; be lost
decisions.reason: Readable explains "eternal life" once in the passage, as the book's terms allow (meaning decision m3). It says "be lost" for "perish", as it does in 3:16.

decisions.choice: arrebatar
decisions.reason: The verb of the wolf in 10:12, so the reader can see the contrast (meaning decision m4). "Perecer / perderse" as at 3:16.

decisions.choice: la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya
decisions.reason: Readable explains eternal life once in the passage (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: ne périront absolument jamais (L); ne périront jamais (B); ne seront jamais perdues (R)
alternatives: ne périront jamais, à aucun moment (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek joins a double negative to "for ever" (meaning decision m2). French "jamais" already says "at no time, for ever", so Balanced needs nothing more; Literal adds "absolument" to show the strength of the double negative. Readable says "perdues", as the English Readable says "lost" (compare 3:16).

decisions.choice: arracher de ma main (every level)
decisions.reason: "Ravir" is the older verb and now usually means "to delight"; "arracher" is the plain word for taking something away by force from someone's grip (meaning decision m4), and it is used again of the Father's hand in verse 29.

decisions.choice: "hư mất" (L, B); "bị mất" (R) for apollymi
decisions.reason: "hư mất" is the established church word for perishing, set against eternal life; R uses the plain "bị mất" (be lost), as the English R does.

decisions.choice: "영원한 생명" at every level; Readable adds "다가올 세상의 생명" once
decisions.reason: The book-wide term (style guide, section 6). "영생" is the familiar contraction; the full phrase keeps "생명" visible as elsewhere in John. Readable explains it once in this passage, as docs/john-terms.md allows.

decisions.choice: arrebatará (L); arrancará (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the wolf in 10:12 (meaning decision m4): taking by force. Literal keeps "arrebatar", the precise word; Balanced and Readable say "arrancar", the everyday word for tearing something out of someone's hand. "Tirar" loses the violence.

source.text: ὁ πατήρ μου ὃ δέδωκέν μοι πάντων μεῖζων ἐστιν, καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται ἁρπάζειν ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ πατρός.

records.literal_gloss: The Father of me, what he has given to me, than all greater is, and no one is able to snatch out of the hand of the Father.

en.L: My Father, as to what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch [them] out of the hand of the Father.
en.B: My Father, who gave them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father's hand.
en.R: My Father is the one who gave them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is greater than anyone or anything. No one can snatch them out of the Father's hand.

es.L: Mi Padre, en cuanto a lo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado, es mayor que todos, y nadie puede arrebatar[las] de la mano del Padre.
es.B: Mi Padre, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} las dio, es más grande que todos, y nadie puede arrebatarlas de la mano del Padre.
es.R: Mi Padre es quien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} las dio, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es más grande que todos y que todo. Nadie puede arrebatarlas de la mano del Padre.

fr.L: Mon Père, quant à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a donné, est plus grand que tous, et personne ne peut [les] arracher de la main du Père.
fr.B: Mon Père, qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} les a données, est plus grand que tous, et personne ne peut les arracher de la main du Père.
fr.R: C’est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} les a données, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est plus grand que tous et que tout. Personne ne peut les arracher de la main du Père.

sw.L: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kuhusu kile alichonipa, ni mkuu kuliko wote, wala hakuna awezaye kuwanyakua kutoka mkononi mwa Baba.
sw.B: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, aliyenipa hao, ni mkuu kuliko wote, wala hakuna awezaye kuwanyakua kutoka mkononi mwa Baba.
sw.R: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ndiye aliyenipa hao, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ni mkuu kuliko mtu yeyote au kitu chochote. Hakuna anayeweza kuwanyakua kutoka mkononi mwa Baba.

vi.L: Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, về điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì lớn hơn tất cả, và không ai có thể cướp [chúng] khỏi tay Cha.
vi.B: Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là Đấng đã ban chúng cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, lớn hơn tất cả, và không ai có thể cướp chúng khỏi tay Cha.
vi.R: Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Đấng đã ban chúng cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lớn hơn tất cả mọi người, mọi vật. Không ai có thể giật chúng khỏi tay Cha.

ko.L: 내 아버지께서는, 내게 주신 것으로 말하자면, 모든 것보다 크시다. 그리고 아무도 아버지의 손에서 [그들을] 빼앗아 갈 수 없다.
ko.B: 그들을 내게 주신 내 아버지께서는 모든 것보다 크시다. 아무도 그들을 아버지의 손에서 빼앗아 갈 수 없다.
ko.R: 그들을 내게 주신 분은 내 아버지시다. 아버지께서는 그 누구보다, 그 무엇보다 크시다. 아무도 그들을 아버지의 손에서 빼앗아 갈 수 없다.

pt.L: O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, quanto ao que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu, é maior do que todos, e ninguém pode [as] arrebatar da mão do Pai.
pt.B: O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, que as deu a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, é maior do que todos, e ninguém pode arrancá-las da mão do Pai.
pt.R: Foi o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai quem as deu a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é maior do que qualquer pessoa ou qualquer coisa. Ninguém pode arrancá-las da mão do Pai.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT reading: neuter "what" with masculine "greater" (ὃ ... μεῖζων)
alternatives: "What my Father has given me is greater than all": neuter "what" with neuter "greater" (Codex Vaticanus in its first hand, and Latin witnesses)
"My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all": masculine "who" with masculine "greater" (papyrus 66, Codex Alexandrinus and most later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ in two small words: "what" or "who", and "greater" in the neuter or the masculine. The SBLGNT follows the mixed reading found in Codex Sinaiticus and a few others, neuter "what" with masculine "greater". Scribes had reason to smooth this harder reading into one of the easier ones, which favors it, but it is hard to construe (meaning decision m2). The reading with both words neuter makes the flock, the Father's gift, the thing that is greater than all; the reading with both masculine makes it the Father. A footnote gives the other readings. A reviewer should check the witnesses against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Father is greater than all; "what he has given me" stands loosely as the object of "has given"
alternatives: take "greater" as if it were neuter: what the Father has given me is greater than all
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT text "greater" is masculine and agrees with "my Father", so the Father is the one who is greater than all. The neuter "what he has given me" is then a loose clause about the sheep, the Father's gift to Jesus, using the same neuter as in 6:37 and 6:39 for all the Father gives him. The sense is: my Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all. The other way of reading it, that the gift itself is greater than all, follows the variant rather than this text.

decisions.choice: no one can snatch them from the Father's hand: the sheep are kept by the Father as by the Son
decisions.reason: Verse 28 said that no one will snatch the sheep out of Jesus's hand; now it is the Father's hand. The reason is that the Father is greater than all, including any who would harm the flock (10:10, 12). The two hands hold the same sheep, which leads into 10:30.

decisions.choice: all: everyone and everything
decisions.reason: The form can be masculine or neuter, so it may mean all people or all things. No power of any kind is greater than the Father.

decisions.choice: as to what he has given me (L); who gave them to me (B, R); them (B, R)
alternatives: what he has given me is greater than all
who has given them to me
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the neuter "what" and shows by "as to" that the Father is the subject of "is greater" (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable say what the clause means: the Father gave the sheep to Jesus. The verb "snatch" has no object in Greek; the sheep are meant, so Literal brackets [them] and the other levels supply it.

decisions.choice: en cuanto a lo que me ha dado (L); que me las dio (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the neuter "lo que" and shows that the Father is the subject (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: que todos y que todo
decisions.reason: The Greek can mean all people or all things (meaning decision m4); Readable says both.

decisions.choice: quant à ce qu’il m’a donné (L); qui me les a données (B, R); plus grand que tous (L, B), que tous et que tout (R)
alternatives: ce qu’il m’a donné est plus grand que tout
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the loose neuter "what" and shows with "quant à" that the Father is the one who is greater (meaning decisions m1, m2); Balanced and Readable say that he gave the sheep to Jesus, so "données" agrees with "brebis". French must choose between "tous" (everyone) and "tout" (everything), where the Greek form can mean either (m4): Literal and Balanced say "tous", since the threat in view is from those who would snatch, and Readable gives both, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" when Jesus speaks of the Father
decisions.reason: The Father is "Ngài" in Jesus's speech as in the narrative, under the same reader setting.

decisions.choice: "내게 주신 것으로 말하자면" (as to what he has given me); "[그들을]"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the loose construction of the SBLGNT reading (see the meaning decision) with the Korean topic phrase "-으로 말하자면"; the object of "snatch" is supplied.

source.text: ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν.

records.literal_gloss: I and the Father one we are."

en.L: I and the Father are one."
en.B: The Father and I are one."
en.R: The Father and I are one."

es.L: Yo y el Padre uno somos».
es.B: El Padre y yo somos uno».
es.R: El Padre y yo somos uno».

fr.L: Moi et le Père, nous sommes un. »
fr.B: Le Père et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, nous sommes un. »
fr.R: Le Père et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, nous sommes un. »

sw.L: Mimi na Baba tu kitu kimoja."

pt.L: Eu e o Pai somos um."
pt.B: Eu e o Pai somos um."
pt.R: Eu e o Pai somos um."

decisions.choice: one: neuter, "one thing", not "one person"
decisions.reason: The word for "one" (ἕν) is neuter. Jesus does not say that he and the Father are one and the same person: he says "we are", in the plural, and the two are named separately. The neuter speaks of a unity between two. John uses the same neuter when Jesus prays that his disciples may be one as he and the Father are one (17:11, 21-22).

decisions.choice: a unity of will and action, which the hearers took as a claim to be God
alternatives: a statement that the Father and the Son are the same person
decisions.reason: In context the unity is shown in what the two do: the same sheep are held in the Son's hand and the Father's hand (10:28-29), and Jesus does the Father's works (10:25, 37-38; 5:19). The hearers took the words as more than agreement: they picked up stones because, they said, "you, being a man, make yourself God" (10:31-33). John does not correct them on that point; he has said that the Word was God (1:1), and Jesus goes on to say that the Father is in him and he in the Father (10:38). The text states the unity without giving a later doctrinal formula for it.

decisions.choice: a possible echo of the confession that God is one
decisions.reason: Israel's confession says that the LORD our God is one (Deuteronomy 6:4). Placing Jesus within that oneness would explain why the hearers reacted as they did (10:31-33). But the words are not a quotation, and the echo may not be intended.

decisions.choice: The Father and I
decisions.reason: English usually names the other person first and "I" last. The Greek order puts "I" first; Literal keeps it. The meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: El Padre y yo (B, R); Yo y el Padre (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: the usual order; Literal keeps the Greek order. Spanish "uno" cannot show the Greek neuter; meaning decision m1 explains it.

decisions.choice: tu kitu kimoja (L); tu wamoja (B, R)
decisions.reason: ἕν is neuter, "one thing", not "one person", as the meaning note says. Literal keeps the neuter with "kitu kimoja"; Balanced and Readable say "tu wamoja" (we are united, at one), which speaks of two persons who are one. "Ni mmoja" would mean one person.

decisions.choice: "Cha và Ta" (B, R); "Ta và Cha" (L)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese courtesy names the other party first, as English does; Literal keeps the Greek order. "là một" keeps the Greek's open "one" without saying "one person".

decisions.choice: "하나" (one), not "한 분" or "한 사람"
decisions.reason: The Greek "one" is neuter: one thing, not one person (meaning decision). Korean "하나" says unity without making the Father and the Son one person.

decisions.choice: Eu e o Pai (every level)
decisions.reason: English puts "I" last for politeness; Portuguese "eu e o Pai" is natural and not felt as self-centred, so every level keeps the Greek order. "Um" is the masculine-neuter form and says "one" without naming a person, as the neuter does (meaning decision m1).
